findings.F1: Among falls of at least one usual move (z ≤ -1; 767 cases), the next-day excess return grows with the raw size of the fall: slope on the day's return -0.32 (t -2.64, clustered by day). The same fall scaled by the 30-day swing gives a slope of -0.012 (t -1.26). With the swing level added, the raw slope stays at -0.37 (t -2.70) and the swing level adds nothing (-0.009, t -0.58). This is why the forecast, graded on the scaled fall, failed its top-minus-bottom check.
findings.F2: Split by quartile of the raw fall, only the deepest quartile rebounds clearly: falls beyond about -9.4 % are followed by +2.07 % excess the next day (t 1.99, 193 cases, 84 days). The other three quartiles give +0.21 % to +0.62 % (t 0.5 to 1.6).
findings.F3: Across all days, the next-day excess return falls as the scaled move rises: slope on z -0.0034 (t -2.37, 6529 cases). Large rises are not mirrored: rises beyond one usual move are followed by -0.14 % to -0.24 % (t -0.15 to -0.70). The effect is one-sided, on falls.
findings.F4: Down days when the coin's 30-day swing is in its top quartile against its own median give +1.22 % excess the next day (t 2.75, 796 cases, 339 days). The three calmer quartiles give +0.24 %, +0.04 % and -0.18 % (t 1.13, 0.19, -0.65). Among falls of at least one usual move, the rebound rises with the swing level: +0.27 %, +0.81 %, +1.39 % by tercile.
findings.F5: Where the day closes in its range adds nothing beyond the day's return. Alone its slope is -0.0117 (t -2.91), but next to the return it drops to 0.0002 (t 0.03) while the return keeps -0.088 (t -2.03). The close-location pattern is the fall itself.
findings.F6: The book's gain per position day grows with the depth of the fall: +0.43 %, +0.43 %, +0.75 % and +2.01 % for z buckets from -1 to below -2.5 (t 1.4, 1.2, 1.5, 1.6). The deepest bucket's rebound is about ten times the 0.19 % cost of a trade.
findings.F7: Other angles did not stand out after counting the more than 20 looked at. These were the weekday of the fall (Thursday +2.56 %, t 2.61, only 42 days), the 60-day trend (rising +1.26 %, t 2.16; falling +0.92 %, t 1.39; choppy -0.36 %), the prior 5-day return, the coin and the 2- and 3-day horizons.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day percentage fall, measured in raw terms rather than against its recent swing, the larger its rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader buying after a sharp daily fall should size the bet by the depth of the fall itself, not by how unusual it is for the coin's recent swing, since the deepest raw falls carry most of the rebound.
ideas.name: raw fall depth next-day rebound

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day fall, the larger its rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader should take the next-day rebound after falls mainly when the coin has been swinging more than usual over the past month, where the give-back is several times larger than in calm markets.
ideas.name: agitated market fall rebound
